subject: Renewal + Midterm Top-up: Bridging Uplift, Co-terming & Sprint Credit Proposal
messages:
From: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@brightlayer.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps Team <procure@brightlayer.ai>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@brightlayer.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + Midterm Top-up: initial ask

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap from BrightLayer's side: Q4 volume is ramping faster than we forecasted (see attached usage CSV). We expect a ~2.3x token increase over the next three months and need a short mid-contract top-up to avoid throttling while we finalize the annual renewal.

Questions we have:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary uplift bucket that sits outside our annual commitment and co-terms to our Jan 31 renewal date?
- Is there a short-term blended rate (we're sensitive to list price) you can offer for the top-up that won't require a full contract amendment?
- Any way to get a small SLA credit if we move some traffic to a lower-tier model for cost control?

We'd like to get something agreed this week so engineering can proceed — happy to sign a one-page amendment if needed.

Best,
Natalie Chen
Head of Platform, BrightLayer AI

Attachments: BrightLayer_Q3_usage_report.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@brightlayer.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + Midterm Top-up: initial ask

Natalie — thanks for the details and the CSV. High level response: we can support a temporary top-up bucket and co-term it to your Jan 31 renewal with a short amendment. Two path options that would be fastest: 

Option A — Bridged Top-up (fast, minimal paperwork)
- Short-lived separate bucket (3–4 months) billed monthly at a blended uplift rate (estimated 18% over your current committed unit price)
- Automatically merges into renewal commitment (pro-rated) at Jan 31 if you choose to annualize
- No change to core SLA; engineering fallback to lower-tier model is possible but SLA credits require legal approval

Option B — Pro-rata Annualize (preferred if you plan to keep the extra capacity)
- Add uplift to current commitment now, pro-rate pricing to Jan 31, then annualize at renewal with a graduated discount ladder (2–4% discount steps depending on volume)
- Requires a short amendment (2–3 business days)

If you want immediate throughput for the next month, Option A gets you enabled in <48 hours. I can draft a one-page amendment and a pricing worksheet for the blended uplift. Ben/Aditya — can you confirm the blended uplift range if we target a 2.3x usage spike and offer a 18–22% uplift vs committed unit price? Priyom — can you prepare a one-page SLA-credit ask for internal legal review (small credit linked to 99.5% availability if they move traffic to lower-tier models)?

I'll attach a draft amendment and pricing worksheet in my next email.

—Kimberly
Director, Renewals — Redwood Inference

Attachments: (none in this message)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal + Midterm Top-up: blended uplift math

Kim / team — quick calc attached (Pricing_worksheet_BRIDGE.xlsx). Notes:
- Baseline committed unit price: $0.0024 / token-equivalent (current contract)
- Projected temporary consumption (next 90 days): +2.3x => incremental tokens = 3,200,000
- Option A blended uplift (monthly billed bucket): 18% uplift => incremental cost ~$13,824 for 90d
- Option B pro-rate to annualize: if customer converts to annualized uplift at renewal, we can offer a 3% step discount on the uplift (effectively 15% vs baseline) provided they commit to the extra volume on renewal.

We should also consider a one-time implementation credit (small) to ease procurement sign-off. I can include a $2,000 credit in the one-pager.

Ben
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Pricing_worksheet_BRIDGE.xlsx

From: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@brightlayer.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps Team <procure@brightlayer.ai>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@brightlayer.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + Midterm Top-up: bridging proposal review

Thanks Kimberly and Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement and engineering:

Procurement: we prefer Option A only if it's explicitly co-termed to Jan 31 and the monthly billing is straightforward (single line item). The one-time $2k credit would help. Can you also confirm any early-termination or carry-forward rules if usage is lower than projected?

Engineering: the temporary bucket needs to be available by Monday; they can route noncritical workloads to the lower-tier model but need assurance the response latency won't exceed 250ms p95 for those calls.

Legal: If we sign the one-page amendment for Option A, will that avoid a broader contract redline?

If you can send the one-pager + the DocuSign link we can route internally and aim to sign by EOD Friday.

—Natalie
Head of Platform

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@brightlayer.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + Midterm Top-up: bridging proposal review

Natalie — thanks, we can do everything you've asked. Final summary and next steps: 

What we will deliver (Option A, one-page amendment):
- Temporary Bridged Bucket (90 days) co-termed to Jan 31, 2027; billed monthly as a single line item
- Blended uplift = 18% over current committed unit price; estimated incremental cost for 90 days ~$13,824
- One-time implementation credit: $2,000 applied to first month invoice
- Carry-forward: unused temporary bucket tokens do not carry forward; if you convert at renewal we will pro-rate actual usage toward the annual commitment (no double-billing)
- SLA note: we cannot promise SLA credits for traffic on lower-tier models in the one-pager; Priyom will draft a separate legal rider for availability credit if you decide to move critical traffic (this will need legal sign-off and will be optional)

Action items: 
- Kimberly: send DocuSign one-pager (attached) — DONE (Draft_Amendment_v1.pdf)
- Natalie: circulate to procurement and legal; target signature by EOD Friday
- Ben: confirm final invoice line item label with Billing ("BrightLayer - Bridged Top-up Sep-Nov 2026")
- Priyom: prepare short legal rider language for SLA-credit request (if they want it post-signature)

I'll include the docuSign link in the follow-up internal note. If signed, engineering will enable the bucket within 48 hours of completed onboarding.

Thanks — looking forward to getting BrightLayer stabilized for Q4.

—Kimberly
Director, Renewals — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_Amendment_v1.pdf
